card: C12-1, selective control (docs/research-log.md, 'Run cards C12-1 and C12-2'; consult 12, direction 1, docs/consults/2026-10-16-practical-ideas/review.md)
label: exploratory (development choices informed by development outcomes, disclosed below; held-out problems first touched by the run test-1)

settings.precision: float32 throughout (stored bf16 weights loaded as float32; logits, softmax and concept tokens in float32)
settings.pipeline: pi_harness soft mode: concept token = top-15 renormalized softmax(z/T)-weighted embedding (pi_harness.concept_token), S soft steps, cue '\n\nThe answer is', 6 greedy answer tokens, pi_harness.extract_answer, exact match of the integer string
settings.task: two-digit additions 'What is a + b?' (a, b in 10..99) wrapped by pi_harness.INSTRUCTION and the chat template (65 prompt tokens for every problem, no padding); 16 development and 64 held-out problems on disjoint unordered operand pairs (docs/pi/c12-1-problems.json)
settings.target_rule: correct + 10 if that keeps the digit count, else correct - 10
settings.objective: teacher-forced log-probability of the target's answer tokens (' ', digits, '.') after the cue
settings.immediate_readout_diagnostic: S = 1: one concept token (perturbed), then the cue; early and late coincide
settings.injections: early = the first concept token e_0; late = the last concept token before the cue, e_{S-1} (the unperturbed prefix is kept)
settings.optimizer_arm: pga20: projected gradient ascent from delta = 0, 20 normalized gradient steps of 2.5 r / 20 (L2 PGD as in Madry et al.), projection onto the ball after each step; the iterate with the largest objective among the 20 is kept (the last iterate's objective costs one forward)
settings.random_search_arm: search: K = 45 random unit directions at the full radius, the one with the largest objective is kept; random1 = the first of these directions; directions seeded by (problem, temperature, horizon, injection, candidate), shared across radii
settings.compute_matching: one gradient pass = c_grad objective evaluations, measured (bench-1, T = 1.0, 32-33 rows): c_grad 1.79 / 1.95 / 2.17 and gradient-path forward 0.93 / 0.95 / 1.18 at S = 16 / 8 / 1, so 20 * c_grad + forward = 36.7 / 40.0 / 44.5 evaluations; K = 45 at every horizon (at least matched; 23 % more than the optimizer at S = 16)
settings.zero_rows: a delta = 0 row per problem in every search and optimizer evaluation batch
settings.forced_target_control: every baseline readout also decoded with +1e4 added to the target's j-th token logit at answer step j
settings.intervals: Wilson 95 % over problem-temperature pairs (descriptive); percentile bootstrap over problems (10,000 resamples) for problem-weighted rates and for every paired contrast

choices.temperatures: Rule fixed before calibrate-2 outputs were seen: among temperatures with development accuracy >= 11/16 at S = 1, 8 and the long horizon, take the largest and the smallest median twin net rate over that horizon (eps 1e-3). Qualifying at S = 16: T = 0.3 (13/16; median rate -0.131 per step, 10 % of twins expanding) and T = 1.0 (11/16; -0.058, 38 %). Both contract at the median; the contrast is modest. T = 0.6 is the most expanding (+0.03 to +0.09 over 20-24 steps) but answers 5/16 at S = 16.
choices.long_horizon: Rule fixed before calibrate-2 outputs were seen: the largest S in {12, 16, 20, 24} at which at least two temperatures reach 11/16 at S = 1, 8 and S. S = 24: only T = 2.0 (13/16); S = 20: only T = 1.0 (11/16); S = 16: T = 0.3 and 1.0. Hence S = 16.
choices.K: bench-1 (T = 1.0; under heavy machine load): c_grad = 1.79 / 1.95 / 2.17 at S = 16 / 8 / 1. For the 5-step optimizer K = 12 (dev staircase); for the 20-step optimizer K = 45 (the largest matched value, 44.5 at S = 1; at least matched at every horizon).
choices.radii: Dose rule fixed before the dev staircase: the smaller dose is the smallest staircase radius (0.01-3) at which the 5-step PGA, early or late, converts >= 25 % of eligible dev pairs, the larger the next radius; if none qualifies, (1, 3). None qualified (best 1/24), so (1.0, 3.0). With the 20-step optimizer the same threshold is first met only at rho = 10 late (13/24); (10, 30) was not adopted: perturbations of 10-30 token norms are outside the question (small perturbations), and the 20-step check was designed as the optimizer positive control, not as the dose staircase.
choices.optimizer: The 5-step PGA (card: 'e.g. 5 steps') failed its positive control on dev (late rho = 1 and 3: 0/24; at most 1/24 at any radius); its objective rose monotonically late (budget-limited) and erratically early. A 20-step L2 PGD (step 2.5 r / 20) passed it (late rho = 10: 13/24; late rho = 3: 5/24) and replaced the 5-step arm for the held-out run.
choices.control_radius: rho = 10 late at S = 16 (the dev positive control that worked with 20 steps: 13/24).

deviations: Horizon S = 32 replaced by S = 16 (and the primary endpoint moved to S = 16). Development accuracy at S = 32 was 1-10/16 at every temperature from 0.3 to 3.0 (calibrate-1; the soft thoughts drift off the question), and at S = 20 or 24 at most one temperature reached 11/16 (calibrate-2). Decided on development baseline outcomes only, before any attack outcome and before any held-out data.

Greedy answer tokens 12 -> 6 (pi_harness default 12). In development baseline texts the model sometimes began to repeat the cue within 12 tokens, and pi_harness.extract_answer, which reads the number after the last 'answer is', then found no number (T = 1.0, S = 32: 2 of 16 problems). Six tokens hold every answer up to four digits with its period. Decided on development baseline texts, before any attack outcome; extract_answer is unchanged.
Immediate-readout diagnostic implemented as S = 1 (one concept token, then the cue); early and late coincide there.
random1 is the first random-search direction, not an independent draw.

Optimizer: 5-step PGA replaced by a 20-step L2 PGD for the held-out run after its positive control failed on development problems (see choices.optimizer); random search K = 45 accordingly. Decided after development attack outcomes, before any held-out data.

Doses (1, 3) from the pre-specified fallback of the dose rule (no staircase radius reached 25 %); the rule applied to the 20-step check would give (10, 30), not adopted (see choices.radii). Decided after development attack outcomes, before any held-out data.
Positive-control radius set to 10 (late, S = 16) on development outcomes.

Temperatures from a development grid (calibrate-1: 0.3-3.0; calibrate-2: 0.3-2.0) with rules written before calibrate-2's outputs; twins at relative 1e-4 and 1e-3 (above the float32 floor; zero-offset twins measure row-position noise).

Every random-search candidate's greedy answer is decoded (descriptive readouts: random answer changes, any-of-K oracle); the selection uses the objective only, and the extra decoding is not counted in the compute matching.

Layout differences measured on the first 8 development problems with batch sizes 8, 4, 1 (planned: 16, 8, 1 on all 16), to shorten the run's tail under heavy machine load; decided before the layout outputs were seen.
The 5-step PGA arm of the card was not run on held-out problems (dev staircase only); the held-out optimizer arm is pga20.
caveats: Exploratory: one small model (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), one task family (two-digit additions), one prompt template, float32 on the CPU.

Both chosen temperatures contract at the median over 16 steps; the finite-time 'expansion' contrast between them is modest. The twin distances show strong contraction in the first steps and later jumps (near-tied top tokens after the soft thoughts have written the answer), not steady exponential growth.
The 5-step optimizer of the card was too weak here; the held-out optimizer (20 steps) and doses were chosen on development outcomes (disclosed).
Rates over 64 problems have about +-12-point worst-case 95 % precision; paired contrasts are bootstrapped over problems.
Radii are relative to the injected token's norm; early (|e_0| ~ 0.33-0.37) and late (|e_15| ~ 0.19-0.55) tokens differ in absolute size; embedding rows have median norm 0.45.

float32 rounding: the zero-offset twin (identical row in the same batch) drifted by up to 1e-5 to 6e-4 relative over 24 steps (calibrate-2), and by up to 1.5e-2 at T = 0.6 over 32 steps (calibrate-1); no zero-perturbation row of any attack batch changed its answer (gated per run).

The held-out matrix took 3.8 h (23:52 to 03:38 PDT; planned about 2.2 h) because the shared CPU's load rose from about 7 to 27 during the run; no configuration was cut, and the whole study (calibration to receipt) took about 6 h.

compute_matching_in_run.definition: seconds per optimizer row (20 gradient passes + 1 forward, test-1) divided by seconds per random-search candidate (its rollout, objective and greedy decoding, test-1): the optimizer's cost in candidates
compute_matching_in_run.note: both measured within the same run under a shared, heavily loaded CPU (load 12-27); random search had at least the optimizer's compute in every configuration even counting its greedy decoding, which the selection does not use

scales.layouts_measured_on: first 8 development problems, batch sizes 8, 4, 1, T = 0.3 and 1.0, S <= 16 (layouts-1)
scales.statement: No radius here is rounding-sized: rho = 1 is about 1e6 times the largest float32 first-token layout difference (1.1e-6), more than 600 times the largest float32 layout difference at any of 16 steps (1.6e-3), and more than 250 times the bfloat16 unit roundoff (3.9e-3); bfloat16 rollouts on this CPU were bitwise identical across batch layouts (the 7B bf16 GPU runs of program PI showed differences around 1e-3 relative, research log PIF64 entry).

problems.target_rule: correct + 10 if that keeps the digit count, else correct - 10

primary.definition: Delta = P(target | pga20) - P(target | search), early injection, S = 16, rho = 1.0, baseline-correct problem-temperature pairs, problems weighted equally, paired bootstrap over problems
